cf.title: standby PANIC on restart after VM truncation

input.subject: PostgreSQL 18.6/17.11: standby PANIC on restart after VM truncation

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The thread states the problem with a reproducer and a field report, and three people confirmed it on four branches. v5 forgets invalid VM pages when truncation is replayed, as XLogTruncateRelation() already does for the main fork, so it follows existing practice. Confidence is medium because the material does not show v5's commit message, file list or code.

brief.title: Fix standby PANIC on restart after visibility map truncation
brief.problem: A standby that already replayed a heap and VM truncation can PANIC with "WAL contains references to invalid pages" when it restarts recovery from an earlier restartpoint. The reporter says it reproduces on 18.6, 17.11, REL_18_STABLE and master, but not on 18.4 or 17.10. It hits after a switchover, and Shihao says also on a plain standby restart with full_page_writes = off.
brief.proposed_design: Two fixes were posted. v4 reads VM pages in the VM-clear redo routines with RBM_ZERO_ON_ERROR and calls PageInit() on a page that comes back zeroed, so wal_consistency_checking still passes. Melanie's v5 keeps RBM_NORMAL and forgets invalid VM pages when truncation is replayed, the way the main fork already does through XLogTruncateRelation().
author_claims: Kirill says the bug goes back to the first VM-clear redo commit, which lacked the invalid page guard that commit defe934 added.
Rahul and Shihao report that v3 and v4 fix the PANIC on master, 19, 18 and 17, with and without wal_consistency_checking.
Rahul found that RBM_ZERO_ON_ERROR alone fails under wal_consistency_checking = all, because heap_mask() rejects an all-zero page.
Shihao says ignore_invalid_pages = on lets an affected standby start until the fix ships.
Shihao reports that v5 lets the standby restart on master, 19, 18 and 17.
brief.thread_state: Melanie posted v5 and prefers the truncation-replay fix, and Shihao accepted it and tested it on four branches. Open items are the v5 test, which does not apply on 17, and updating the CommitFest entry, which still points at the v4 approach.
unclear: The material does not show v5's commit message or file list, so its scope and backpatch range are not visible.
No message explains why 18.4 and 17.10 pass while 18.6 and 17.11 fail, given Kirill's claim that the bug is older.
No message says whether v5 also covers the DELETE, HOT update and cross-page update cases that the v4 test checks.
Nobody says whether v5 passes with wal_consistency_checking = all.
No message says which test should go in on 17, where the v5 test does not apply.

committability.owner_note: Melanie Plageman wrote v5 and prefers the truncation-replay fix; the owner needs to know the visibility map redo code and invalid-page tracking in recovery.
committability.liability: The owner signs for recovery correctness of VM truncation replay on master and every back branch that gets the fix, for the life of those branches.
committability.author_follow_up: Shihao accepted v5 and tested it on master, 19, 18 and 17; Rahul tested the earlier versions on the same branches.

priority.reason: A standby PANIC on restart in released minor versions affects users of streaming replication, and v5 reuses the main-fork mechanism without new user-visible surface. Review cost is medium because no fix patch was read and the change is in recovery code that goes to stable branches.

provisional_note: The material shows only the v1 test patch, so v5's code, commit message and file list were not judged. Whether forgetting invalid VM pages at truncation replay could hide a real invalid-page reference cannot be checked without the code.

precedents_retrieved.title: Write visibility map during CLUSTER/VACUUM FULL
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make CLUSTER and VACUUM FULL write the visibility map during heap rewrite, by having rewriteheap.c build VM pages alongside heap pages (bypassing the buffer manager) and flush them to smgr. It used its own simplified all-visible check, relying on HeapTupleSatisfiesVacuum() having already set hint bits; TOAST relations were left without a VM.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected to copying visibility-map implementation details into rewriteheap.c and to adding another copy of visibility-determination logic, which he said has proven hard to get right. He also questioned part of the motivation and pointed to related prior discussion that might share logic, especially for TOAST. The author did not respond to these comments for over two months, and the entry was marked returned with feedback.
matched_queries: visibility map truncation redo invalid pages
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I don't think we should have yet another copy of logic determining
visibility. It has repeatedly proven hard to get right in the past, and
it'll not get better by having yet another copy.

precedents_retrieved.title: Write visibility map during CLUSTER/VACUUM FULL
precedents_retrieved.authors: Alexander Korotkov (smagen), Justin Pryzby (justinpryzby), Anna Akenteva (anna.akenteva), Anna Akenteva (a.akenteva)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes CLUSTER and VACUUM FULL write the visibility map in heapam_relation_copy_for_cluster(), so the table needs no extra VACUUM afterwards. VM pages are built in RewriteStateData beside the heap pages and written straight to smgr, with an all-visible check that assumes tuples already passed HeapTupleSatisfiesVacuum().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The original author stopped responding, and no one took ownership of the patch. In 2019 the entry was returned with feedback because review comments went unanswered for more than two months. After a 2021 revival, Justin Pryzby kept rebasing it and asked for an owner, then proposed closing it, and the entry was marked returned with feedback in 2022. Open points included Amit Kapila's question about syncing VM pages at end_heap_rewrite and Justin Pryzby's note that pg_class.relallvisible is not set.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I'm planning to close this patch until someone can shepherd it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
Reverted commit(s): Track conflict_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Till now, the reason for replication slot invalidation is not tracked
directly in pg_replication_slots. A recent commit 007693f2a3 added
'conflict_reason' to show the reasons for slot conflict/invalidation, but
only for logical slots.

This commit adds a new column 'invalidation_reason' to show invalidation
reasons for both physical and logical slots. And, this commit also turns
'conflict_reason' text column to 'conflicting' boolean column (effectively
reverting commit 007693f2a3). The 'conflicting' column is true for
invalidation reasons 'rows_removed' and 'wal_level_insufficient' because
those make the slot conflict with recovery. When 'conflicting' is true,
one can now look at the new 'invalidation_reason' column for the reason
for the logical slot's conflict with recovery.

The new 'invalidation_reason' column will also be useful to track other
invalidation reasons in the future commit.

precedents_retrieved.title: OFFSET optimisation for IndexScan using visibility map
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch pushed OFFSET information down to index scans, so tuples on all-visible pages that the Limit node would throw away were skipped without heap fetches. The author later reworked it into a general "Index Only Fetch Scan", which evaluates filter quals from index data and fetches heap tuples only for rows it returns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier marked it returned with feedback because the author promised an update in July and did not post one by October. Heikki Linnakangas objected to the redesign: evaluating expressions on index entries of deleted tuples can raise errors, such as division by zero, before the visibility check filters those entries out. The author also had no cost estimation that would avoid a 3-4% slowdown for high-correlation, low-selectivity cases. Tom Lane's review of predicate locking appears only in quoted lines.
matched_queries: visibility map truncation redo invalid pages
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Now, maybe there's some way around that, but I don't know what. Without some kind of a solution, this won't work.

precedents_retrieved.title: Track Oldest Initialized WAL Buffer Page
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an OldestInitializedPage field to XLogCtl that tracks the start address of the oldest initialized WAL buffer page, updated under WALBufMappingLock. Its purpose is to let callers check quickly, without a lock, whether a WAL record is still in the WAL buffers, and to walk the buffers from oldest to newest.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas showed that a caller can already check whether a record is in WAL buffers by comparing xlblocks[idx] with the expected page end pointer, with an atomic read if stale results are fine. He saw no need to track OldestInitializedPage. The author did not reply, and the entry was returned with feedback after the thread stalled.
matched_queries: WAL contains references to invalid pages
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
But I don't see the point of tracking OldestInitializedPage. It
seems cheap enough that we could, if there's a need for it, but I don't
see the need.

precedents_retrieved.title: Don't keep closed WAL segment in page cache after replay
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch calls POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED on a WAL segment before a standby closes it after replay, so replayed WAL does not stay in the page cache. Later versions skip this when archive_mode = always, WAL summarization, active walsenders or used replication slots need the WAL, using atomic counters for the last two checks.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund doubted the benefit and noted that no measurements were posted. He argued that the kernel replaces clean page cache pages cheaply, and that dropping them makes crash restarts, reading 2PC state from WAL and base backups more expensive. He asked for convincing benchmarks first; the visible messages end there, and the entry was withdrawn.
matched_queries: WAL contains references to invalid pages
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think you'd have to have pretty convincing benchmarks showing that this is a
good idea before we should even remotely consider applying this.

precedents_retrieved.title: Optimize walsender handling invalid messages of 'drop publication'
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes how walsender handles invalidation messages from 'drop publication' on releases before PG 14, which lack the XLOG_XACT_INVALIDATIONS record type. pgoutput stops doing needless cache invalidation, and a relid-to-relfilenode hash map replaces a hash sequential search; the patch targets REL_13_STABLE and back branches only.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No one reviewed the patch for four months. Andres Freund then objected that users hitting the issue should upgrade, and that performance improvements are rarely backpatched, and not when they would go only into back branches without first maturing in the development branch. The author later withdrew the entry.
matched_queries: WAL contains references to invalid pages
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's one thing to decide to backpatch an
optimization if it had time to "mature" in the development branch, but from
what I undestand you're proposing to apply this just to the back branches.

precedents_retrieved.title: Don't ignore recovery conflict interrupt on blocked writing
precedents_retrieved.summary: On a standby, a backend blocked writing results to a stuck or dead client ignores interrupts, so its buffer pin can block WAL replay until the TCP retransmission timeout, which can be about 15 minutes. The patch makes ProcessClientWriteInterrupt() handle recovery conflict interrupts during a blocked write and terminate the session, with a new Perl module for raw protocol tests.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund found that the patch did not promote the ERROR to FATAL, so the session was not really terminated. He also showed that the backend often reaches ProcessClientWriteInterrupt() with interrupts held, for example while sending an error message, and then the conflict is never resolved. The author posted a reworked approach on 2025-01-21. No reply follows in the visible messages, and they do not say why the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Unfortunately I suspect that this means any protection we'd get from this version of the patch is rather incomplete - if the recovery conflict is triggered while not blocked, we'll ERROR out and report the message with interrupts held.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
Reverted commit(s): Add redo LSN to pgstats files
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit b860848232aa, that was added as a prerequisite for
the support of pgstats data flush across checkpoints, linking a pgstats
file to a specific checkpoint redo LSN.

As reported, this is proving to be currently problematic when going
through a pg_upgrade, that does direct manipulations of the control file
in the new cluster.  The LSN stored in the pgstats file is not able to
cope with any changes done in the control file by pg_upgrade yet,
causing the pgstats file to be discarded when starting the new cluster
after overriding its redo LSN (one is a `pg_resetwal -l` where the new
cluster's start LSN is bumped by a hardcoded value of 8 segments, see
copy_xact_xlog_xid).

The least painful path going forward is likely going to be a refactor of
the pgstats code so as it is possible to read and write some of its data
with some routines in src/common/, so as pg_upgrade or pg_resetwal are
able to update its data.  The main point is that we are going to need a
LSN in the stats file should we make it written at checkpoint time and
not only as part of a shutdown sequence.  It is too late to dive into
these details for v18, so let's revert the change, and let's try to
figure out all the details in the next release cycle.  The pgstats file
is currently only written as part of a shutdown sequence, and its
contents are still lost on crash, same as older releases.

Bump PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found, and none of the retrieved candidates is the same or a similar idea. The thread points only to related work that is still open: commit defe934 (message #2), which added the main-fork invalid page guard that v5 now extends to the VM fork, and Melanie's VM clear thread (messages #3 to #5), which v5 replaces.

From the standards and compatibility angle there is nothing to object to. Both v4 and v5 change only WAL redo behaviour for visibility map pages, with no new syntax, GUC, catalog entry, pg_dump output, psql change or client-visible behaviour. The backpatch to 17 changes no user-facing contract. The open items are choosing between v4 and v5, wal_consistency_checking coverage for v5, and a test for 17. These are design and test questions for other angles.

This is a redo-only bug fix. It does not change the on-disk format, WAL record layout, catalogs, wire protocol or extension ABI, so pg_upgrade and mixed-version standbys are not affected. v5 forgets invalid VM pages when truncation is replayed, the same way XLogTruncateRelation() already does for the main fork, which follows existing practice. Questions only: why 18.4 and 17.10 pass, and whether v5 passes with wal_consistency_checking = all.

Both fixes change only how the startup process replays visibility map pages during recovery, and they add no new privilege, role, setting or user-visible surface. Any user who can vacuum a table can trigger the PANIC today, and both fixes remove that; the ignore_invalid_pages workaround is already superuser-only.

This is a back-patchable fix for a standby PANIC, and a committer who knows the visibility map code, Melanie Plageman, wrote v5 (message #10). v5 handles VM truncation replay the same way the main fork already does through XLogTruncateRelation(), so it adds no new mechanism, GUC, catalog change or hot-path cost for users who do not hit the bug. The open items are which test goes into 17 and whether v5 is checked under wal_consistency_checking = all and against the DELETE and update cases in the v4 test (messages #3, #11); those are test questions outside this angle.

This is a recovery bug fix, and no existing feature removes the PANIC. ignore_invalid_pages = on, named in message #3, is a temporary workaround that turns off a safety check, so it does not replace the fix. The thread has moved to v5, which reuses the main-fork forget-invalid-pages path in XLogTruncateRelation() and does not add a second mechanism.

This is a bug fix for a recovery PANIC in released minor versions. A field report on Linux, a reproducer, and independent confirmation on four branches by three people show the problem is real. A committer engaged and posted a fix. A demand objection does not apply to a crash on standby restart.
